topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture topic on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of innate pathogen and damage recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system identifies infections and cellular damage using conserved molecular patterns and germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor systems and inflammatory signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail major pattern recognition receptor families, their intracellular signaling pathways, and the activation of the inflammasome.

topics.label: Acute inflammatory response and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cell activation directs leukocyte extravasation into tissues, lymphatic drainage, and systemic inflammatory consequences like sepsis.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the mechanisms for resolving acute inflammation, repairing tissue damage, and managing persistent inflammatory states or granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the next topic.
